names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 30 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιοι Τέρτιος, Μάρκος, Ιούστος και Αρτεμάς οι Απόστολοι από τους Εβδομήκοντα», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the title on his name link behind the line for 30 октября ст. ст., «Святитель Артема, епископ Листрийский, апостол от 70-ти», with the rank words and the see left off. The line itself declines the name, «Артемы».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 30. октобар ст. ст., „Св. ап. Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем.“ — «Св. ап.» is "saint" plus the `apostle` grade, and the other four names are the heading’s other members, so the bare personal name is the whole of the form. The heading gives him no see: «епископ у Листри Ликаонској» is the body’s, and the folder carries «Bishop of Lystra» in `office`. `foldchk.py` finds the string on `artemas-of-cyzicus`, so the form joins a fold of two, keyed in `READ_FOLDS` in the same commit. This is also the folder’s FIRST name form outside Greek and Russian.

feast.note: The Greek calendar keeps the same four apostles on its own 30 October; this is the Russian calendar's own day and not a second day on one calendar. His name page was not opened; the line and the life of the four are what this row rests on.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 30 октября ст. ст. — «Апп. от 70-ти Тертия , Марка , Иуста и Артемы (I).»
source.note: The line is the second of the day. The day carries one typikon sign only, «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком», so no rank is recorded.

attestations.note: The Russian agrees with the Greek line this folder was written from, and its one life for the four adds the province and the death: «Святой Артема был епископом в ликаонском городе Листре; скончался мирно» — bishop in the Lycaonian city of Lystra, and he fell asleep in peace. The name link behind the line titles him «Святитель Артема, епископ Листрийский, апостол от 70-ти», a hierarch's rank word the Greek page did not give him; the folder's `types` keep the line's own word, «Апп.», apostle, and the see goes in `office`.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (1 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 30ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιοι Τέρτιος, Μάρκος, Ιούστος και Αρτεμάς οι Απόστολοι από τους Εβδομήκοντα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 30 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry enumerates four apostles of the Seventy, each with his own heading and his own see, so it is four folders in principle; two of them the corpus already keeps and this is a new one. **It is not the corpus's Artemas of Cyzicus**, who is a martyr with a Greek feast on 28 April and a Romanian one on 29 April; this Artemas is an apostle of the Seventy who became bishop at Lystra. The page records fragments of his relics at the monasteries of Mega Spilaio at Kalavryta and of Kykkos in Cyprus. No year, so no `dates` object. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 12.11.2025 (30. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. ап. Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, fifth and last of the five apostles it enumerates. THE HEADING ENUMERATES FIVE APOSTLES — «Клеопа, Терције, Марко, Јуст и Артем» — so the brief’s enumeration ruling makes it one folder per named member, and all five rows quote the whole heading. FOUR of the five take a row here. THE FIFTH, Марко, TAKES NOTHING: `mark-of-byblos` already carries a venerated serbian row out of this same book’s Julian 27 September, where it identifies him in the same words this entry does, and section 1 makes a saint already venerated on another day report-only. The reading is in the commit message. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW. «ап.» is the `apostle` the folder holds; the body says «Св. Артем био епископ у Листри Ликаонској, и мирно скончао» — he was bishop in Lystra of Lycaonia AND ENDED PEACEFULLY. So NO `martyr` was added to him, where `martyr` WAS added to `tertius` and to `justus-of-eleutheropolis` in this same commit off this same heading. ONE HEADING, FIVE APOSTLES, AND THE BODY GIVES THEM FOUR DIFFERENT ENDS: Cleopas nothing at all, Tertius martyred at Iconium, Mark nothing, Justus suffering at Eleutheropolis, Artemas asleep in peace at Lystra. A rank word in a heading governs a company; a death in a body belongs to one man. `dates` UNTOUCHED: `death` 1 to 100 off the Russian «(I)», and this entry gives no year. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: the peaceful end, which is the only statement about his death this folder has from any source, and «Ликаонској» — of Lycaonia — beside the see the `office` already carries as «Bishop of Lystra». NO `related` — this folder has none and this entry names nobody with him. No `locations`. THE FORM FOLDS AND THE FOLD IS KEYED: «Артем» is already held by `artemas-of-cyzicus`, a `martyr` of the third century, so this takes the key from one holder to two. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day’s verse is Bishop Nikolai’s own and is about king Milutin.

death.note: days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 30 октября ст. ст. closes the four apostles with «(I)», the first century, and its life for them gives no year. The folder held no `dates` before this; saint.gr gave him none.
